description: The plot illustrates how vocabulary size grows as the number of iterations increases, shown separately for three languages (Spanish, Korean, Japanese) with multiple runs per language and an additional diagonal reference line. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Iterations,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 500 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, and 500. The y-axis is labeled “Vocabulary Size,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 to 5000 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, and 5000. A gray solid diagonal line runs from approximately (0, 0) to (500, 5000). For Spanish, there are several faint blue solid curves plus a darker blue solid curve (the prominent/average-looking line); the blue curves start near 0 at iteration 0 and rise steadily, reaching roughly the low-to-mid 3000s by iteration 500 (the darker blue line ends around ~3300). For Korean, multiple faint orange solid curves and a darker orange solid curve similarly rise from near 0 at iteration 0, increasing almost linearly and ending around roughly ~3100–3200 at iteration 500 (the darker orange line appears near ~3100). For Japanese, multiple faint green solid curves and a darker green solid curve rise from near 0 at iteration 0 and continue upward to around the low-to-mid 3000s by iteration 500 (the darker green line ends around ~3250). Across all three languages, the curves show a smooth, steadily increasing trend over the full x-range without visible drops, with the faint per-run curves closely clustered around each language’s darker curve.
